evidence.text: The entry analyzes the bronze form of 送 as 辵 plus phonetic 灷. It says 辵 contributes the walking sense; 灷 is also the initial graph in the 送、媵、賸 series and served as their phonetic element. It describes the small-seal 灷 shape as a graphic alteration, and quotes Shuowen: “送，遣也。从辵，㑞省。𨕼，籒文不省.” This supports a phonetic-semantic analysis and identifies Shuowen’s account as a historical analysis, rather than confirming Shuowen’s component identification as the only explanation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

evidence.field: 形義通解；中山王圓壺引文
evidence.text: The entry reports that a bronze graph in the Zhongshan king round pot is read as 朕 (“I, my”), quoting “隹(唯)送(朕)先王” and attributing the reading to Zhang Zhenglang. This is a reading of the graph in that inscription, distinct from the verb 送’s graphic analysis; the entry does not establish that every form of 送 was borrowed for the pronoun.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

The date of the poem’s composition and the precise semantic distinction between seeing someone off and accompanying them are not resolved by this result.

evidence.text: For the proposed sound component 灷 (U+7077), the entry calls it the phonetic element in 送 and says its bronze shape derives from 廾 plus 丨 with decorative dots, later graphically altered in small-seal writing. It does not provide a historical pronunciation comparison for 灷 and 送, and its statement about phonetic function is not itself a reconstruction. A secondary result reports modern 灷 as zhuàn, but no verified Unicode Unihan row or comparable historical reading was retrieved.

The CUHK entry asserts that 灷 serves as phonetic in 送, 媵 and 賸 and explains a small-seal graphic alteration, but the inspected page does not provide a dated earliest attestation or fully independent paleographic argument. No image was visually inspected.

The received Shijing quotation is an early literary attestation, but this research did not establish a precise composition date or a chronology for later senses such as give, dispatch, deliver and escort. Do not infer chronological development from dictionary gloss ordering.
